name: Libni
overview: Libni was a male member of the tribe of Levi, uniquely identified as the son of Gershon. He is associated with the Libnites, a clan named after him, indicating his role as a patriarch within the Levitical families. His mention in Scripture situates him within the priestly lineage important for the service of God.
namesAndTitles: The name Libni means 'white' in Hebrew, reflecting perhaps a characteristic or symbolic meaning attributed to him or his descendants. He is also referred to as Ladan in 1 Chronicles 23:7, though no specific meaning is provided for this name. Neither name is indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Libni as the son of Gershon. Inferred relationships include Jahath and Jehiel as his fathers in different genealogical accounts, and Zetham and Joel as his ancestors, demonstrating the complexity of Levitical genealogy. These connections anchor Libni firmly within the Levitical priestly lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Libni's significance lies in his role as the progenitor of the Libnites, a Levitical clan responsible for specific duties in the tabernacle service. His lineage through Gershon places him within the tribe entrusted with sacred responsibilities, underscoring the continuity of God's covenantal promises through the Levitical priesthood. Thus, Libni contributes to the biblical narrative by representing the faithful transmission of priestly heritage.
